title: Sovereign routing stakeholder roster and handoff procedures
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures an operationally-focused stakeholder roster and step-by-step handoff procedures for implementing sovereign (region-pinned) routing requests from customers. It is intended to be used by Solutions Eng, Customer Success, Ops, and SRE when coordinating enforcement, telemetry, and audit evidence for region pins or temporary exemptions. Draft — expect edits and heavier detail in linked runbooks.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted + dedicated + private deployment modes where customer traffic or persisted data needs to be anchored to a geographic region (country/region level).
- Covers request intake, engineering handoff, short-term exemptions, audit evidence packaging, and post-migration verification.
- Does NOT replace legal contract clauses; use Legal for contract-level commitments.

Quick summary of intent:
- Reduce ambiguity on who does what for a region-pin request.
- Ensure evidence collected is auditable (logs, traces, routing snapshots).
- Define a repeatable, quick handoff so SLAs for onboarding and enforcement are predictable.

Stakeholder roster (roles + primary contacts):
- Customer Success (CS): primary onboarding lead — owns customer comms and acceptance criteria. (Primary: Sofia Romero)
- Solutions Engineering (SE): validates technical requirements, runs preflight tests, composes deployment checklist. (Primary: Liam Chen)
- Platform Engineering / Routing Owner: implements routing policy changes (route tables, edge ACL, region pin config). (Primary: Priya Kapoor)
- SRE / Oncall: monitors rollout, exposes fallback, responsible for rollback plan. (Pager: eng-oncall)
- Compliance / Legal: signs off on evidence package for audits and contract obligations. (Reviewer: Asha Patel)
- Security / Infosec: reviews KMS/HSM usage and encryption boundary questions. (Reviewer: TBD)
- Customer Engineering (if applicable): installs customer-side VPN/proxy bits for private deployments.

Handoff trigger events (when to run this flow):
- New customer signs contract requiring region residency (e.g., data-at-rest + inference in EU-only).
- Customer requests pinning via support escalation (ticket label: residency-pin).
- Incident requires temporary regional exemption or emergency local routing.

Intake checklist (CS/SE):
- Confirm contract clause and exact scope (storage, inference, logs, telemetry) — copy to ticket.
- Ask: which tenant ids/paths need pinning? Provide sample request body.
- Desired go-live date and hard deadlines for compliance audits.
- Acceptable fallback policies (e.g., fallback to nearest region vs. degrade to read-only).
- Provide point of contact for 24/7 coordination windows.

Technical preflight (SE + Platform):
- Map customer tenant -> logical routing key (tenant_id, account_id).
- Confirm model variants available in target region or approved fallback model set.
- Verify capacity (GPU/instance) in target region for expected QPS + burst.
- Validate storage anchor: is object store, DB, or ephemeral cache required to be in-region? Determine replication config.
- Identify third-party integrations (logging, metrics, monitoring) that might cross borders and propose mitigations.

Execution / engineering handoff (Platform):
1) Create an implementation branch/PR describing exact config changes (include PR link in ticket).
2) Add routing policy entry: specify selector, destination region(s), precedence, and TTL for temporary exemptions.
3) Apply change to staging (staging tag: residency-pin-<tenant>). Run end-to-end tests: routing traces, KV cache locality check, end-to-end latency smoke.
4) Collect telemetry snapshot (pre-change): routing table snapshot, sample request traces (obfuscated), metrics baseline.
5) Create canary deployment for a small percentage of traffic (5%). Observe 1-2 business days depending on SLA.
6) Gradually ramp to 100% per escalation plan.

Evidence & audit packaging (required items):
- Routing table snapshot (timestamped).
- Trace spans showing request path stayed within target region (anonymize user PII).
- Storage allocation records showing data-at-rest location.
- Deployment PR + changelog.
- Capacity verification (instance ids / reservation ids if Dedicated).
- Confirmation email to customer + acceptance signoff.

Telemetry to record (events & tags):
- residency.pin.requested (ticket id, tenant_id, requested_region)
- residency.pin.implemented (PR id, commit sha, applied_by)
- residency.pin.verification (evidence_bundle_id)
- residency.pin.exemption.issued (reason, expires_at)

Temporary exemptions (fast path):
- Use when capacity constraints or urgent incident requires brief deviation.
- Exemption must include TTL (max 72 hours unless escalated), owner, and rollback plan.
- Exemption application flow: SE/Platform approval -> SRE applies route override with TTL -> create evidence snapshot -> notify Compliance.

Escalation matrix & SLAs:
- CS initial triage: < 4 business hours
- SE preflight complete: 2 business days (unless priority flagged)
- Platform PR + staging verification: 3 business days (normal)
- Emergency exemption response: 1 hour to acknowledge, 4 hours to implement if feasible
- Compliance evidence packaging: 2 business days after implementation

Communication templates (short):
- To customer: "We received your residency pin request for <tenant>. Next step: technical preflight scheduled by Solutions Eng on <date>. We will share verification artifacts after roll out."
- Internal Slack channel naming: #residency-<tenant>-<region> (create ephemeral channel for coordination)

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Who is final approver for exemptions longer than 72 hours? (Legal + Product?)
- Standardize naming for evidence bundles (suggestion: residency-evidence-<tenant>-<YYYYMMDD>-<uuid>).
- Automate trace collection into Confluence or evidence bucket — backlog item: PRIV-861.

Action items (next steps):
- SE (Liam): draft a preflight template API request body and attach to this doc.
- Platform (Priya): prototype script to snapshot routing table and push to S3 evidence bucket.
- CS (Sofia): create customer-facing onboarding checklist and update onboarding playbook.

Notes to self / quick reminders (informal):
- Keep data samples sanitized when attaching traces.
- When in doubt, escalate to Compliance — better to get sign-off early.
- For private/on-prem installs, define handshake checklist (networking, DNS, certs) earlier than usual — these trips up timelines.

References & links:
- Sovereign Routing Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Sovereign+Routing+Spec
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284
- Open JIRA: PRIV-742 (residency automation backlog)

Last edited by: Asha Patel
